subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Roles and Responsibilities
subdomains.objective: To ensure that roles and responsibilities are defined for all parties participating in implementing the cloud cybersecurity controls, including the roles and responsibilities of the head of the CSP and CST or his/her delegate, referred to in these controls as the “Authorizing Official”.

controls.desc: In addition to ECC control 1-4-1, the Authorizing Official shall also identify, document, and approve the following:
Cybersecurity roles and RACI assignment for all stakeholders of the cloud services, including the Authorizing Official’s roles and responsibilities.
controls.evidence: • Cloud Cybersecurity Roles and Responsibilities and RACI matrix documented and approved within the related Service Level Agreements (SLAs) between the CSP and CSTs.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Risk Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure cybersecurity risks are managed using a methodological approach in order to protect the CSP’s and CSTs’ information and technology assets in accordance with organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: The cybersecurity risk management methodology mentioned in ECC Subdomain 1-5 shall also include for the CSP, as a minimum:
Defining acceptable risk levels for cloud services and clarifying them to the CST when the risk is related to the CST.
controls.evidence: • Defined acceptable risk levels of cloud services documented and communicated with the concerned and relevant stakeholders, including the CSTs.

controls.desc: Considering data and information classification in the cybersecurity risk management methodology.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity Risk Management Methodology that includes a clear procedure for dealing with data based on its classification levels.

controls.desc: Developing a cybersecurity risk register for cloud services and monitoring it periodically according to the risks.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity Cloud Services Risk Register.
• Cybersecurity Cloud Services Risk Register review plan.
• Cybersecurity Cloud Services Risk Register review reports.

subdomains.title: Compliance with Cybersecurity Standards, Laws and Regulations
subdomains.objective: To ensure that the CSPs’ and CSTs’ cybersecurity program complies with related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to ECC control 1-7-1, the CSP’s legislative and regulatory compliance shall include, as a minimum, the following requirement:
Continuous compliance with all laws, regulations, instructions, decisions, regulatory frameworks and controls, and mandates regarding cybersecurity in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
controls.evidence:
• List of all laws, regulations, instructions, decisions, regulatory frameworks and controls, and cybersecurity mandates applicable to the CSP in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
• Reports clarifying the status of compliance with these requirements.
• Reports clarifying periodic plans for monitoring compliance.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity in Human Resources
subdomains.objective: To ensure that cybersecurity risks and requirements related to personnel (employees and contractors) are managed efficiently prior to employment, during employment, and after termination or separation in accordance with organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC controls 1-9-3 and 1-9-4, the following requirements shall be covered prior to and during the professional relationship of personnel with the CSP, as a minimum:
Positions of cybersecurity functions in the CSP’s data centers within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia shall be filled with qualified and suitable Saudi nationals.
controls.evidence:
• List of cybersecurity positions related to data centers within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the requirements for each position.
• List of employees filling these positions and their qualifications.
• Cybersecurity training program and the training certificates provided under the program.

controls.desc: Screening or vetting candidates and personnel working within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia who have access to the Cloud Technology Stack, periodically.
controls.evidence:
• Screening/Vetting process defined and implemented for candidates with access to the Cloud Technology Stack, including a plan for periodic screening/vetting.
• Screening/Vetting reports for these candidates, with information privacy and sensitivity considered.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity policies shall be a prerequisite for access to the Cloud Technology Stack and shall be signed and appropriately approved.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity policies acknowledgement and compliance form signed by all personnel working on the Cloud Technology Stack before access is granted.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 1-9-5, the following requirement shall be in place, as a minimum, for termination or completion of a human resource’s professional relationship with the CSP:
Assurance that assets owned by the organization, especially those with security exposure, are accounted for and returned upon termination.
controls.evidence: • Signed clearance forms that include employees’ acknowledgement to return all organization assets, validated by the concerned department.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity in Change Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure that cybersecurity requirements are included in change management methodology and procedures in order to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and technology assets in accordance with the CSP’s policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for change management within the CSP shall be identified, documented, and approved.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity change management policy approved by the organization.
• Formal approval by the head of the organization or his/her deputy on the policy.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for change management within the CSP shall be applied.
controls.evidence:
• Documents confirming the implementation of cybersecurity requirements for change management, as documented in the policy.
• Document that clarifies an action plan for implementing cybersecurity requirements for change management.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity for change management in the CSP shall cover, as a minimum:
Processes and procedures to securely implement planned changes in production systems, with priority given to cybersecurity observations.
controls.evidence:
• Change management procedures that prioritize implementation of changes related to cybersecurity.
• Evidence demonstrating verification of secure procedures during execution of changes.

controls.desc: A process for implementing exceptional cybersecurity changes, such as changes during incident restoration.
controls.evidence:
• Document containing procedures for implementing exceptional changes.
• Evidence demonstrating technical capability for monitoring and controlling changes.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for change management within the CSP shall be applied and reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence:
• Log of updates and changes to the cybersecurity requirements for change management.
• Approved document that sets the policy review schedule.
• Policy indicating that it has been reviewed and updated and that changes have been documented and approved.
• Formal approval by the head of the organization or his/her deputy on the updated policy.

subdomains.title: Asset Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure that the CSP and CST have an accurate and detailed inventory of information and technology assets in order to support the organization’s cybersecurity and operational requirements and maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and technology assets.

controls.desc: In addition to the controls in ECC control 2-1, the CSP shall cover the following additional controls for asset management, as a minimum:

Inventory of all information and technology assets using suitable techniques, such as a Configuration Management Database (CMDB) or a similar capability containing an inventory of all technical assets.
controls.evidence:
• Asset inventory techniques identified and utilized.
• Document outlining the inventory of technical assets specific to cloud systems.
• Organization information and technology asset information maintained within an asset inventory, such as a CMDB.

controls.desc: Identifying asset owners and involving them in the asset management lifecycle.
controls.evidence:
• Document outlining the asset inventory and the owners assigned to the assets.
• Evidence demonstrating that the roles and responsibilities of asset owners are aligned with their respective assets.

subdomains.title: Identity and Access Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure secure and restricted logical access to information and technology assets in order to prevent unauthorized access and allow only authorized access necessary to accomplish assigned tasks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-2-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for identity and access management, as a minimum:
Identity and access management of generic account credentials for which accountability cannot be assigned to a specific individual.
controls.evidence:
• Document outlining the list of users of generic accounts, including service and technical accounts.
• Technical restrictions applied to the use and management of generic accounts.

controls.desc: Secure session management, including session authenticity, session lockout, and session timeout termination.
controls.evidence: • Evidence demonstrating configurations applied to sessions, including authenticity, lockout, and timeout.

controls.desc: Multi-factor authentication for privileged users and personnel candidates with access to the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• List of privileged accounts with access to Cloud Technology Systems (CTS).
• Multi-factor authentication technologies implemented for privileged accounts with access to Cloud Technology Systems.

controls.desc: A formal process to detect and prevent unauthorized access, such as unsuccessful login-attempt thresholds.
controls.evidence:
• Authentication and monitoring of access.
• The number of allowed access attempts is limited and the account is temporarily closed when the limit is exceeded.
• Sample system configuration and monitoring report.
• Access-attempt alerts.

controls.desc: Utilizing secure methods and algorithms for saving and processing passwords, such as secure hashing functions.
controls.evidence:
• Evidence demonstrating a sample of stored passwords.
• Document outlining the standard applied to password storage.

controls.desc: Secure management of third-party personnel accounts.
controls.evidence:
• Restrictions implemented for third-party accounts based on approved standards.
• Procedures adopted for managing third-party accounts during their lifecycle.
• Sample third-party account requests showing the necessary approvals.
• Sample third-party account activity-monitoring logs.
• Defined labels for third-party accounts.
• Implemented Federated Identities and Authentication.
• Third-party account and privilege review plan and reports.

controls.desc: Access control enforced for management systems and administrative consoles.
controls.evidence:
• List of management systems and administrative consoles.
• Sample requests for access to management systems and administrative consoles.
• Access privilege review plan and review reports for management systems and administrative consoles.
• Evidence of using Privileged Access Management (PAM) technology.
• Evidence of encryption for access communications through the network and a list of activated encryption algorithms.
• Evidence of Multi-Factor Authentication implementation.
• Sample event monitoring and related alerts from a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system.
• Sample recording of sessions.

controls.desc: Masking displayed authentication inputs, especially passwords, to prevent shoulder surfing.
controls.evidence: • Evidence demonstrating implementation of obfuscation and masking of sensitive and personal information.

controls.desc: Obtaining the CST’s approval before the CSP or a CSP third party accesses any CST-related asset or data.
controls.evidence:
• Approved procedures for requesting access to the CST’s assets or data.
• Sample approval requests.

controls.desc: Capability to immediately interrupt a remote access session and prevent any future access for a user.
controls.evidence:
• Controlled remote access sessions established.
• Sample system or proxy configurations.

controls.desc: Provision to CSTs of multi-factor authentication services for privileged cloud users.
controls.evidence: • Evidence demonstrating that cloud services are authenticated using multi-factor authentication.

controls.desc: Assurance of restricted and controlled access to storage systems and storage means, such as Storage Area Networks (SAN).
controls.evidence:
• Access policy for storage systems.
• Asset register containing storage systems.
• Sample access-policy implementation for storage systems.
• Sample architecture design of storage systems.
• Sample access requests for storage systems.

subdomains.title: Information System and Information Processing Facilities Protection
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of information systems and information processing facilities, including workstations and infrastructure, against cyber risks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-3-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for information system and processing facilities protection, as a minimum:
Ensuring that all configurations are applied in accordance with the CSP’s cybersecurity standards.
controls.evidence:
• Approved cybersecurity standards for information systems.
• Checklist for applying standards to configurations before deployment and before changes are applied.
• Review plan for information system configurations and review reports.
• Sample event logs for monitoring configuration changes.
• Restrictions applied to configuration modification and the list of personnel permitted to change configurations.
• Sample configuration-change requests.

controls.desc: Assurance of separation and isolation of data, environments, and information systems across CSTs to prevent data commingling.
controls.evidence:
• Verified separation of data and systems across CSTs.
• Test reports validating the prevention of data commingling.

controls.desc: Adopting cybersecurity principles for technical system configurations according to the minimum-functionality principle.
controls.evidence:
• Minimum-functionality requirements defined for the configuration and functionality of technologies, systems, software, and services.
• Configuration audit reports demonstrating compliance with the specified requirements.

controls.desc: The ability of the Cloud Technology Stack to securely handle input validation, exceptions, and failures.
controls.evidence:
• Sample configuration for input validation.
• Sample evidence of automatic monitoring and logging to capture exceptions and failures.
• Evidence confirming logging and monitoring of alerts and audit reports.

controls.desc: Full isolation of security functions and applications from other functions and applications in the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• Document demonstrating that security functions and applications are isolated from other functions and applications in the Cloud Technology Stack.
• Architecture design documentation.

controls.desc: Notifying CSTs of cybersecurity requirements provided by the CSP and applicable for use by CSTs.
controls.evidence:
• Document describing the cybersecurity requirements provided by the service provider and methods of activating them on subscriber services.
• Evidence demonstrating communication to subscribers of requirements that can be activated upon request.

controls.desc: Detection and prevention of unauthorized changes to software and systems.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity requirements for change management.
• Evidence confirming applied restrictions that prevent, detect, and remediate unauthorized changes.
• Evidence illustrating system configurations for change-prevention tools.
• Change monitoring reports or alerts.

controls.desc: Complete isolation and protection of multiple guest environments.
controls.evidence:
• Guest environments isolated.
• Architectural design document for hosting environments illustrating isolation.
• Sample virtual-environment threat model.
• Sample test report.

controls.desc: Community cloud services provided to CSTs, including government and Critical National Infrastructure organizations, shall be isolated from any other cloud computing provided outside the scope of work.
controls.evidence:
• Architectural design documentation.
• Sample isolation mechanisms implemented between cloud services provided to government and sensitive-infrastructure entities and cloud services provided to other external entities.

controls.desc: Providing cloud computing services from within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including systems used for storage, processing, and disaster recovery centers.
controls.evidence:
• Cloud data centers located in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
• Architectural design document for storage systems, processing systems, and disaster recovery centers, including their geographical locations and whether they are leased or owned.
• Evidence illustrating the addresses of the centers’ locations.

controls.desc: Providing cloud computing services from within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including systems used for monitoring and support.
controls.evidence:
• Evidence that cloud-computing monitoring and support centers are based in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
• Architectural design document for storage systems, processing systems, and disaster recovery centers, including their geographical locations.
• Sample contracts showing whether facilities are leased or owned.
• Evidence illustrating the addresses of the centers’ locations.

controls.desc: Modern technologies, such as Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), shall be used to ensure that the CSP’s information servers and processing-system devices are ready for rapid response to incidents.
controls.evidence:
• EDR systems implemented across all devices and servers.
• EDR system configuration review plan and reports.
• EDR system update plan and reports.

subdomains.title: Networks Security Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of the CSP’s and CSTs’ networks from cyber risks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-5-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for network security management, as a minimum:
Monitoring traffic across external and internal networks to detect anomalies.
controls.evidence:
• Inventory of network flows.
• Anomaly-detection rules defined on detection tools.

controls.desc: Network isolation and protection of the Cloud Technology Stack network from other internal and external networks.
controls.evidence:
• Threat model for the Cloud Technology Stack network.
• Network-level controls implementation.
• Architecture design documentation.

controls.desc: Protection from denial-of-service attacks, including Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS).
controls.evidence: • Document or report demonstrating that denial-of-service threats are analyzed, detected, and mitigated.

controls.desc: Protection of data transmitted through the network to and from the Cloud Technology Stack using strong cryptographic mechanisms for management and administrative access.
controls.evidence: • Evidence illustrating that Cloud Technology Stack management networks are strongly encrypted.

controls.desc: Access control between different network segments.
controls.evidence:
• Network connections assigned to authenticated users or identities.
• Access-control list.

controls.desc: Isolation between the cloud service delivery network, cloud management network, and CSP enterprise network.
controls.evidence:
• Isolation mechanisms for networks.
• Architecture design documentation.

subdomains.title: Mobile Devices Security
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of mobile devices, including laptops, smartphones, and tablets, from cyber risks and ensure secure handling of the CSP’s and CSTs’ information, including sensitive information, while using mobile devices.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-6-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for mobile device security, as a minimum:
Inventory of all end-user and mobile devices.
controls.evidence:
• Maintained inventory of end-user and mobile devices.
• Periodic review reports.

controls.desc: Centralized mobile-device security management.
controls.evidence:
• All mobile devices centrally managed from a security perspective.
• Sample system configuration.

controls.desc: Screen locking for end-user devices.
controls.evidence:
• Screen-lock policy enforced on user devices.
• Documents illustrating user-awareness methods for manually locking screens when users are away from their devices.

controls.desc: Data sanitization and secure disposal for end-user devices, especially devices exposed to the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence: • Approved and implemented data-sanitization and device-disposal tools and methods for end-user devices related to the Cloud Technology Stack.

subdomains.title: Data and Information Protection
subdomains.objective: To ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the CSP’s and CSTs’ data and information in accordance with organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-7-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for data and information protection, as a minimum:
Prohibiting the use of Cloud Technology Stack data in any environment other than the production environment, except after applying strict controls such as data masking or data scrambling.
controls.evidence:
• Production data segregated from test data.
• Architecture design documentation.

controls.desc: Providing CSTs with secure data-storage processes, procedures, and technologies to comply with related legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.evidence:
• List of applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
• Data-storage processes and technologies compliant with legal requirements.

controls.desc: Disposal of CST data shall be performed securely upon termination or expiry of the contract with the CSP.
controls.evidence:
• Contract-status monitoring.
• Records of disposed CST data specifying the disposal methods used.

controls.desc: Commitment to maintain the confidentiality of CST data and information in accordance with related legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.evidence: • Evidence that storage and processing of CST data are subject to applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

controls.desc: Providing CSTs with secure means to export and transfer data and virtual infrastructure.
controls.evidence: • Secure data and asset export functionality over an encrypted and secure channel or connection.

subdomains.title: Cryptography
subdomains.objective: To ensure the proper and efficient use of cryptography to protect information assets in accordance with policies, procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-8-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for cryptography, as a minimum:
Technical mechanisms and cryptographic primitives for strong encryption in accordance with the advanced level of the National Cryptographic Standards (NCS-1:2020).
controls.evidence: • NCS-1:2020-compliant data-encryption mechanisms.

controls.desc: Certification authority and certificate-issuance capability shall be implemented securely, or certificates shall be issued by a trusted certification authority.
controls.evidence:
• Installation and activation of a trusted source or authority for accreditation.
• Trusted and certified certificates.

subdomains.title: Backup and Recovery Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of the CSP’s data and information, including information systems and software configurations, from cyber risks in accordance with organizational policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-9-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for backup and recovery management, as a minimum:
Securing access, storage, and transfer of CST data backups and their media and protecting them against damage, amendment, or unauthorized access.
controls.evidence:
• List of identified risks.
• Defined and applied security measures.
• Regular review reports.

controls.desc: Securing access, storage, and transfer of Cloud Technology Stack backups and their media and protecting them against damage, amendment, or unauthorized access.
controls.evidence:
• List of identified risks.
• Defined and applied security measures.
• Regular review reports.

subdomains.title: Vulnerability Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure timely detection and effective remediation of technical vulnerabilities to prevent or minimize the probability of exploiting them to launch cyberattacks against the CSP and CST.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-10-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for vulnerability management, as a minimum:
Assessing and remediating vulnerabilities on external components of the Cloud Technology Stack at least monthly, and internal components at least every three months.
controls.evidence:
• Threat and Vulnerability Management Policy.
• Sample vulnerability assessments.
• Sample remediation plans and actions.

controls.desc: Notification to CSTs of identified vulnerabilities that may affect them and the safeguards in place.
controls.evidence: • Reports sent to CSTs regarding detected vulnerabilities that affect them.

subdomains.title: Penetration Testing
subdomains.objective: To assess and evaluate the efficiency of the CSP’s cybersecurity defense capabilities through simulated cyberattacks to discover unknown weaknesses within the technical infrastructure that may lead to a cyber breach.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-11-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrol for penetration testing, as a minimum:
The scope of penetration tests shall cover the entire Cloud Technology Stack and the tests shall be conducted at least once every six months.
controls.evidence: • Penetration tests conducted across the entire Cloud Technology Stack.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Event Logs and Monitoring Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure timely collection, analysis, and monitoring of cybersecurity event logs for proactive detection and effective management of cyberattacks to prevent or minimize the impact on the CSP’s and CSTs’ business.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-12-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for cybersecurity event logs and monitoring management, as a minimum:
Activating and protecting event logs and audit trails of the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• Log management policy.
• Centralized and protected log repository.

controls.desc: Activating and collecting login-attempt history.
controls.evidence:
• Stored and recorded login attempts.
• Evidence illustrating mechanisms for verifying login attempts.

controls.desc: Activating and protecting all event logs of activities and operations performed by the CSP at the tenant level to support forensic analysis.
controls.evidence: • CSP and CST event or activity logs.

controls.desc: Protecting cybersecurity event logs from alteration, disclosure, destruction, unauthorized access, and unauthorized release in accordance with regulatory or legal requirements.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity event logs protected.
• Restrictions applied to protect the logs.
• Secure log-destruction methods.
• List of legal and regulatory requirements for audit logs.

controls.desc: Continuous cybersecurity event monitoring using SIEM technology covering the full Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity logs monitored in a SIEM system.
• List of requirements for cybersecurity event monitoring.
• Sample monitoring reports or alerts.

controls.desc: Reviewing cybersecurity event logs and audit trails periodically, covering CSP events in the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity event logs reviewed by skilled and independent reviewers.
• Sample reports, alerts, or use cases.

controls.desc: Automated monitoring and logging of remote-access session event logs.
controls.evidence: • Remote-access sessions automatically monitored.

controls.desc: Secure handling of user-related data found in audit trails and cybersecurity event logs.
controls.evidence: • Personally Identifiable Information anonymized in logs.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Incident and Threat Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure timely identification and detection of cybersecurity incidents, effective incident management, and proactive response to cybersecurity threats to prevent or minimize impacts on the CSP’s business.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-13-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for cybersecurity incident and threat management, as a minimum:
Subscribing to authorized and specialized organizations and groups to stay up to date on cybersecurity threats, common practices, and key know-how.
controls.evidence:
• List of trusted external threat-intelligence vendors.
• Cybersecurity threat intelligence.
• Knowledge base of common and best practices in cybersecurity.

controls.desc: Training employees and third-party personnel to respond to cybersecurity incidents in accordance with their roles and responsibilities.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity training program aligned with the roles and responsibilities of the target groups.
• Sample training certificates or attendance records.

controls.desc: Periodically testing the cybersecurity incident-response capability.
controls.evidence:
• Incident response plan or procedure test schedule.
• Report outlining the methodology for testing cybersecurity incident-response capabilities.
• Lessons-learned records.

controls.desc: Performing root-cause analysis of cybersecurity incidents and developing plans to address the findings.
controls.evidence:
• Root-cause analysis established as a mandatory part of incident response.
• Root-cause analysis conclusions prioritized and addressed.
• Incident response plan continuously improved based on root-cause analysis conclusions.
• Sample root-cause analysis.

controls.desc: Supporting the CST in legal proceedings and forensics while protecting the chain of custody under the CSP’s management and responsibility.
controls.evidence:
• Evidence demonstrating knowledge and understanding of legal and regulatory requirements for CSTs.
• Legal and forensic capabilities established.
• Movement of evidence tracked and evidence integrity ensured.

controls.desc: Real-time reporting to the CST of incidents that may affect the CST when an incident is discovered.
controls.evidence:
• Impact on CSTs analyzed for all identified incidents.
• Incidents affecting CSTs immediately reported to the CSTs with sufficient information.
• Sample incidents reported to CSTs.

controls.desc: Supporting CSTs in handling security incidents in accordance with the agreement between the CSP and CST.
controls.evidence:
• Incident-handling process agreed between the CSP and CST and formally recognized in the contract.
• Process established for reporting incidents affecting CSTs.

controls.desc: Measuring and monitoring cybersecurity incident metrics and monitoring compliance with contracts and legislative requirements.
controls.evidence:
• Contractual and legislative requirements register.
• Formally approved and tested cybersecurity incident metrics, including KPIs and KCIs.
• Metrics dashboards and compliance reports.
• Records of dashboard and compliance-report reviews.
• Sample dashboard and compliance report.

subdomains.title: Physical Security
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of the CSP’s information and technology assets from unauthorized physical access, loss, theft, and damage.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-14-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for physical security, as a minimum:
Continuous monitoring of access to the CSP’s sites and buildings.
controls.evidence:
• Inventory of site and building gates and access points.
• Documentation of defined attack vectors, access-monitoring requirements, and the access-monitoring process.
• Access logs and records.
• Access-log and record reviews.

controls.desc: Preventing unauthorized access to devices in the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• Closed physical perimeter for servers and data storage with access-control points.
• Devices locked in secure racks to prevent damage and insertion of external portable devices.

controls.desc: Secure disposal of cloud infrastructure hardware and storage equipment.
controls.evidence:
• Applicable legal regulations and best practices for hardware disposal.
• Formally approved cloud infrastructure hardware-disposal policy.
• Hardware-disposal records and tracking system.

subdomains.title: Web Application Security
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of the CSP’s external web applications from cyber risks.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 2-15-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrol for web application security, as a minimum:
Protecting information involved in application-service transactions against risks such as incomplete transmission, misrouting, unauthorized alteration, and unauthorized disclosure.
controls.evidence:
• Web application firewalls appropriately configured.
• Traffic inspection and behavioral monitoring established.
• Access from known malicious or bad-reputation sources denied.
• Data-transmission encryption and integrity-protection layer, such as TLS/SSL, applied.
• Regular review of application exposure to the Internet and detection of unintentional data exposure.
• Default or common application passwords denied.
• Detection of malicious or unintentional routing-table changes or service redirections implemented.
• Ongoing transaction monitoring established.

subdomains.title: Key Management
subdomains.objective: To ensure secure management of the CSP’s and CSTs’ cryptographic keys to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and technical assets.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for the key management process within the CSP shall be identified, documented, and approved.
controls.evidence:
• Key Management standard formally approved and periodically reviewed.
• Regular review reports.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for the key management process within the CSP shall be applied.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity requirements for the key management process implemented and followed in accordance with the defined policy and related documentation.

controls.desc: In addition to ECC subcontrol 2-8-3-2, cybersecurity requirements for key management within the CSP shall cover, as a minimum:
Ensuring well-defined ownership for cryptographic keys.
controls.evidence: • Identified cryptographic keys and assigned owners.

controls.desc: A secure cryptographic-key retrieval mechanism in case a cryptographic key is lost, such as backup and trusted key storage strictly external to the cloud.
controls.evidence: • Cryptographic-key retrieval plan.

controls.desc: Logging and monitoring key-management activities.
controls.evidence:
• Comparison of the list of active cloud services with the list of monitored cloud services.
• Sample SIEM reports, alerts, or use cases.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for key management within the CSP shall be applied and reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence:
• Cybersecurity requirements for Key Management reviewed periodically.
• Periodic review logs.

subdomains.title: System Development Security
subdomains.objective: To ensure that cybersecurity requirements for system development within the CSP are identified, documented, approved, applied, and reviewed periodically.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for system development within the CSP shall be identified, documented, and approved.
controls.evidence: • Cybersecurity requirements for system development formally approved and periodically reviewed.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for system development within the CSP shall be applied.
controls.evidence:
• Enforced cybersecurity requirements for system development.
• Document outlining implementation of the compliance-measurement tool for the standard.
• Documents defining violation-escalation procedures.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for system development within the CSP shall include, as a minimum:
Considering cybersecurity requirements of the Cloud Technology Stack and relevant systems in the design and implementation of cloud computing services.
controls.evidence:
• Sample compliance review.
• Applied cybersecurity requirements.

controls.desc: Protecting system-development environments, testing environments, including data used for testing, and integration platforms.
controls.evidence:
• List of identified risks.
• Evidence confirming identification of preventive measures and protection of data used in the testing environment.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for system development within the CSP shall be applied and reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence:
• Current cybersecurity requirements for system development.
• Sample periodic reviews.

subdomains.title: Storage Media Security
subdomains.objective: To ensure the CSP’s secure handling of information and data on physical media.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for the use of information and data media within the CSP shall be identified, documented, and approved.
controls.evidence: • Information and Data Media Usage Standard.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for the use of information and data media within the CSP shall be applied.
controls.evidence: • Information and data media labeled, securely stored, and securely disposed.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for the use of information and data media within the CSP shall cover, as a minimum:
Enforcement of media sanitization prior to disposal or reuse.
controls.evidence: • Media-sanitization tools in use.

controls.desc: Using secure means when disposing of media.
controls.evidence: • Defined requirements and acceptable methods for disposal of media.

controls.desc: Maintaining confidentiality and integrity of data on removable media.
controls.evidence:
• List of identified risks.
• Defined controls and requirements for data on removable media.
• Regular review reports.

controls.desc: Human-readable labeling of media to identify its classification and the sensitivity of the information it contains.
controls.evidence:
• Established labeling rules.
• Each media item labeled according to the established rules.

controls.desc: Secure storage of removable media.
controls.evidence:
• List of identified risks for storing removable media.
• Controls and requirements for secure storage of removable media.

controls.desc: Restriction and control of portable-media use inside the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• List of identified risks for using external storage media on the Cloud Technology Stack.
• Approved restrictions and controls for using external storage media on the Cloud Technology Stack.

controls.desc: Cybersecurity requirements for the use of information and data media within the CSP shall be applied and reviewed periodically.
controls.evidence:
• Current cybersecurity requirements for the use of information and data media.
• Periodic review logs.

subdomains.title: Cybersecurity Resilience Aspects of Business Continuity Management (BCM)
subdomains.objective: To ensure inclusion of cybersecurity resilience requirements within the CSP’s and CSTs’ business continuity management and to remediate and minimize impacts on systems, information processing facilities, and critical e-services from disasters caused by cybersecurity incidents.

controls.desc: In addition to the subcontrols in ECC control 3-1-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for cybersecurity resilience aspects of business continuity management, as a minimum:
Developing and implementing disaster recovery and business continuity procedures in a secure manner.
controls.evidence:
• Disaster Recovery Procedure or Plan for cloud computing.
• Business Continuity Procedure or Plan for cloud computing.

controls.desc: Developing and implementing procedures to ensure resilience and continuity of cybersecurity systems dedicated to protecting the Cloud Technology Stack.
controls.evidence:
• Document outlining enhanced measures to ensure resilience and continuity of cybersecurity systems dedicated to protecting the Cloud Technology Stack.
• Periodic review reports and documents.
• Evidence illustrating techniques and methods ensuring resilience and continuity.

subdomains.title: Supply Chain and Third-Party Cybersecurity
subdomains.objective: To ensure the protection of assets against cybersecurity risks related to third parties, including outsourcing and managed services, in accordance with policies and procedures, and related laws and regulations.

controls.desc: In addition to implementing ECC controls 4-1-2 and 4-1-3, the CSP shall cover the following additional subcontrols for third-party cybersecurity requirements, as a minimum:

Ensuring that the CSP fulfills NCA requests to remove software or services provided by third-party providers that may be considered a cybersecurity threat to national organizations from the marketplace provided to CSTs.
controls.evidence:
• Review of the catalogue of third-party software providers and their software.
• Document outlining procedures for removing specific software from the marketplace based on legislative requests.

controls.desc: Requirement to provide security documentation for equipment or services supplied by suppliers and third-party providers.
controls.evidence:
• Security documentation for equipment or services from suppliers and third-party providers.
• Periodic review reports and documents.

controls.desc: Third-party providers shall comply with laws and regulatory requirements relevant to their scope.
controls.evidence:
• Relevant laws and regulatory requirements identified for each third-party provider.
• Proof of compliance with laws and regulatory requirements for each third-party provider.

controls.desc: Risk management and security governance for third-party providers shall be incorporated into general cybersecurity risk management and governance.
controls.evidence:
• Third-party risks embedded in Risk Management processes.
• Sample risk register that includes identified third-party risks.
